findings.quote: Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000.
findings.rationale: Mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, mutual exclusion of indirect damages, and Excluded Claims covering confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. Payment obligations are expressly not damages. Meets our preferred position.

findings.quote: Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
findings.rationale: Vendor IP indemnity plus breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure and procure/modify/refund remedies; Customer's indemnity is narrow. Meets our preferred position.

findings.quote: Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory.
findings.rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds Customer; the agreement expressly preserves our freedom to operate.

findings.quote: Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
findings.rationale: This is exclusive dealing for the full three-year term with no performance-based exit, which is walk-away territory for us and also contradicts Section 12.3. We propose deleting it; if some protection is needed we can accept exclusivity for a defined product category for 12 months, ending automatically on any service-level failure.

replacement.oldText: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We cannot commit to sole-supplier status; our position is no exclusivity, and this clause also conflicts with Section 12.3. Fallback if needed: a defined product category, 12 months only, terminating automatically on Vendor's failure to meet service levels.

findings.quote: Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
findings.rationale: This is an open-ended MFN running against us, requiring us to extend Vendor the best terms given to any other supplier — our walk-away case. MFN in our favour is welcome; an obligation on us is not. We propose deletion.

replacement.oldText: 7.2 Customer shall offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms Customer offers any other technology supplier.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We do not grant MFN obligations to suppliers, and an undefined "best terms" obligation is unworkable across our supplier base. Deleted; happy to discuss MFN pricing in Customer's favour instead.

findings.quote: For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
findings.rationale: One-sided, 18 months post-termination, covers every Vendor employee at any time during the term, includes "engage" (an effective no-hire) and has no general-advertising carve-out. That fails our fallback on scope, duration and carve-outs, and conflicts with Section 12.3. Narrowed to a mutual 12-month solicitation restriction limited to personnel involved in the Services.

replacement.oldText: 12.4 For eighteen months after termination Customer will not solicit or engage any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term.
replacement.newText: 12.4 During the term and for twelve months after the end of a person's involvement in the Services, neither Party will solicit for employment any personnel of the other Party who were directly involved in performing or receiving the Services. This does not restrict general advertisements or recruitment campaigns not specifically targeted at such personnel, responses to unsolicited approaches, or the hiring of any person so identified.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We accept only a narrow, mutual, 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel involved in the Services, with a general-advertising carve-out and no no-hire. As drafted this also conflicted with Section 12.3.

findings.quote: 9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable.
findings.rationale: Section 9 provides only termination for cause, insolvency and Vendor default. There is no Customer right to terminate for convenience in a three-year term, which is a deviation. We have added a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund; fallback is 60–90 days' notice.

replacement.oldText: 9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.
replacement.newText:
9.5 Termination of one Order Form does not terminate another Order Form unless Customer states that the affected Services are operationally inseparable. A termination right is in addition to, and does not exclude, any other remedy available under this Agreement or Applicable Law.

9.6 Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination and no early-termination charge or penalty will apply.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We require a convenience exit on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund in any multi-year term; our fallback is 60–90 days' notice.

findings.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
findings.rationale: A 180-day non-renewal notice window exceeds our 90-day walk-away threshold and well exceeds the 60-day fallback. The 12-month renewal term and the CPI/3% uplift cap in 8.3 are acceptable; only the notice window needs to change.

replacement.oldText: 8.2 Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives one hundred eighty days' advance written notice.
replacement.newText: 8.2 Each Order Form renews for twelve months unless either Party gives thirty days' advance written notice.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] A 180-day non-renewal window is far outside our tolerance; we need 30 days, and can live with 60 as a fallback.

findings.quote: This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles.
findings.rationale: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County; no arbitration. Matches our preferred position.

findings.quote: Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
findings.rationale: Customer has an affiliate/successor carve-out, Vendor assignment requires our consent and can never go to a competitor, and Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination or repricing right. Meets our preferred position.

findings.quote: Upon creation and subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Customer owns each Deliverable created specifically for Customer. Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables
findings.rationale: Customer owns Customer Data and Deliverables with a Vendor assignment, Vendor Technology embedded in Deliverables is covered by the perpetual licence in 13.2, and joint ownership is excluded. Meets our preferred position.

findings.quote: Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services
findings.rationale: Affiliates and contractors are covered, paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable, transfer to an Affiliate or successor is permitted, and suspension is limited to uncured material breach after notice. Meets our preferred position.

findings.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
findings.rationale: Unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems is our walk-away case, and it directly contradicts the no-system-access language in 22.2. Rewritten to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor, no system access; cost allocation in 22.2 already meets our position.

replacement.oldText: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
replacement.newText: 22.1 No more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice and during normal business hours, Vendor may, through an independent auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations, verify Customer's usage of the Services. Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer's systems remotely or directly, and any audit must be conducted so as not to unreasonably disrupt Customer's operations.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] Audits must be annual, noticed, off-site and conducted by an independent auditor; unannounced audits and remote system access are not acceptable. This also aligns 22.1 with the access limits already in 22.2.

findings.quote: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
findings.rationale: An uncapped daily liquidated-damages charge on us, triggered by any dependency delay however minor, is outside our position — we do not pay liquidated damages or penalties. We propose deletion; Vendor's remedy should be relief from affected timelines.

replacement.oldText: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
replacement.newText: 7.6 If Customer's delay in providing an agreed dependency actually delays Vendor's performance, Vendor's sole remedy is an equitable extension of the affected timelines and recovery of reasonable, documented, unavoidable costs directly caused by the delay.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer, particularly uncapped daily amounts for minor delays; schedule relief plus documented costs is the appropriate remedy.

findings.quote: For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. Hosted Services will conform throughout the subscription term.
findings.rationale: Professional/workmanlike warranty, 90-day Deliverable conformance plus term-long hosted conformance, no-malicious-code and compliance-with-law warranties, and a re-perform/repair/replace/refund remedy that the disclaimer expressly does not swallow. Meets our preferred position.

findings.quote: commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 aggregate, workers' compensation as required by law, employer's liability of USD 1,000,000, professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000
findings.rationale: Coverage lines and limits match our preferred position, with certificates on request and no limitation of Vendor's liability.

findings.quote: No minimum quantity or purchase commitment applies. Customer pays only for Services ordered in a mutually executed Order Form, and its decision not to enter another Order Form is not a breach or shortfall.
findings.rationale: No minimum commitment or take-or-pay; fees are for ordered Services only, and Vendor cannot add minimum-use charges. Meets our preferred position.

findings.quote: Upon expiry or termination for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at the rates in the expiring Order Form.
findings.rationale: Six months of transition assistance, data return within 30 days in a machine-readable format with no fee-dispute holdback, and certified deletion only after confirmed return. Meets our preferred position.
